overview: This batch finalizes the simulation loop by implementing deterministic state hashing for save/load integrity, optimizing the tick-based physics solver for 100% Monte Carlo survival, and introducing a lightweight psychological state machine for colonist morale. These atomic tasks close the final coverage gaps in the Deep-Mantle simulation core.

tasks.title: Deterministic State Hashing for Save/Load Integrity
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a zero-heap, constexpr-friendly FNV-1a hash for the core simulation state struct. Use std::array for fixed-size state buffers. Ensure no dynamic allocation during hashing. The hasher must be stable across compiler versions (C++20 standard). Integrate with the existing TickManager to verify state consistency after every 100 ticks. Handle endianness explicitly using std::endian.
acceptance_criteria: Hash computation completes in < 1 microsecond for 10k entities.
Zero heap allocations during hashing phase.
Identical state produces identical hash across 3 different compiler versions (MSVC, Clang, GCC).
Unit tests cover edge cases: empty state, max-size state, and partial updates.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Ensures save games are never corrupted, providing a reliable and fast resume experience.

tasks.title: Optimized Tick-Based Collision Solver for 10k Entities
tasks.architectural_spec: Refactor the collision detection loop to use a spatial hash grid with fixed-size buckets (std::array). Implement a sweep-and-prune algorithm for 1D axis alignment before 2D checks. Use SIMD intrinsics (SSE4.2/AVX2) for bounding box intersection tests. Ensure the solver is stateless and operates on contiguous memory blocks. Max 60 lines of logic per function.
acceptance_criteria: No false positives in collision detection.
Memory footprint remains constant regardless of entity count (within grid limits).
Passes all 16,500 logged footsteps from BATCH-41 without deadlock.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Smooth 60 FPS performance even with large colonies, preventing stutter during complex interactions.

tasks.title: Lightweight Colonist Morale State Machine
tasks.architectural_spec: Implement a 3-state finite state machine (Idle, Working, Panicked) for colonist morale. Use a bitfield for state storage to minimize memory. Transitions are driven by tick-based events (e.g., 'Food Shortage', 'Nightfall'). No dynamic strings; use enum indices for state names. Integrate with the existing TickManager for synchronous updates.
acceptance_criteria: State transitions occur within 1 tick of event trigger.
Memory usage per colonist < 16 bytes for morale state.
No cascading header dependencies; self-contained module.
Visual feedback in UI reflects state changes instantly.
tasks.player_fun_impact: Provides clear, immediate feedback on colony status, enhancing strategic decision-making.
